title: Design System: Frederick Akam, Product Engineer

display.purpose: The name in the first viewport; the closing question at one notch down.

statement.purpose: The risk sentence alone, on a dark ground.

section.purpose: Section heads after the engine, followed by a hairline to the right edge.

headline.purpose: Engine layer headings, one per frame.

body.purpose: Ledger detail in soft ink at a 62ch measure.

label.purpose: Gauge and spec labels, uppercase mono.

numeral.purpose: The records total; all numbers are mono with tabular figures.

shadows.name: button
shadows.purpose: Pinned Email me button at rest.

shadows.name: button-hover
shadows.purpose: Pinned Email me button on hover.

shadows.name: button-ask
shadows.purpose: Closing Email me button on the ink band.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: The drawn data sheet resting on a dark ground.

shadows.name: shot-hover
shadows.purpose: Ledger screenshots on hover, with a 3px rise.

shadows.name: bar-glass
shadows.value: background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--bone) 90%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule)
shadows.purpose: The bar once the reader is past the engine. Not a shadow; recorded here as the bar's only depth treatment.

motion.name: exp
motion.purpose: State transitions that move or scale: bar name 0.45s, button press 0.25s, gauge tick 0.4s, screenshot lift 0.5s.

motion.name: colour
motion.purpose: Colour, underline and background changes on links, buttons, gauge labels and the bar.

motion.name: scroll-map
motion.purpose: Maps scroll progress to sheet lift, copy crossfade and ground tone, after a 0.3 dwell per unit.

motion.name: engine-unit
motion.purpose: One scroll unit per layer, plus the opening frame and a 0.4 unit hold.

motion.name: sheet-lift
motion.value: translateY(-108vh) rotate(-5deg), fade over the last 30%
motion.purpose: How a sheet leaves the pile.

motion.name: pile-depth
motion.value: 16px lower and 4% smaller per sheet, max 3 visible; resting tilt 1.6, -1.2, 1 deg
motion.purpose: Depth by position in the engine.

motion.name: copy-handover
motion.purpose: Engine copy hands over as the top sheet clears.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: The records total runs 0 to 5,880,000 on reaching DATA.

motion.name: lenis
motion.purpose: Smooth wheel scroll; never created under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions 0.01ms, no Lenis, engine not pinned
motion.purpose: Stacked fallback with every layer readable.

narrative.overview:
The page is a desk with one job's drawings stacked on it. The ground is warm bone paper, the type is ink, and the product sheets are whiter than the desk so they read as paper resting on paper. Scrolling down is digging down: after the opening frame, each 100svh lifts the top sheet off the pile and the ground underneath falls one step toward ink, so depth reads twice, as position in the pile and as tone in the ground. The register is exact, calm and checkable: every claim sits next to a capture, a number or a URL.

Density changes on purpose. The pinned engine is sparse, one heading, one paragraph and one sheet per frame, with a five-tick gauge on the edge so the reader always knows how deep they are. Everything after the engine is a dense ledger on bone: hairline-ruled rows, mono spec lists, live URLs, and a closing ask on ink. The system prefers a rule to a box, a measured number to an adjective, and a real capture to an illustration.

Confirmed rejections: the project-card grid, the 3D-corridor showreel the previous page used, generated imagery of any kind, and a second accent colour.
keyCharacteristics: Warm OKLCH neutrals (hue 60 to 80) running from bone to ink, with one burnt-oxide accent.
Three type voices with fixed jobs: Newsreader for names and claims, IBM Plex Sans for explanation, IBM Plex Mono for anything measured.
A pinned five-layer engine with a lit gauge, a falling ground and a sheet pile that lifts one sheet per scroll unit.
Ledger rows separated by hairlines instead of cards.
Soft, warm, downward paper shadows; radius only on pills, sheets and screenshots.
Real captures only, each captioned with its source; data drawn in HTML.

rules.name: The Two Targets Rule
rules.body: Oxide marks the lit gauge tick and the Email me button, and nothing else. Its only other appearances are states: the focus ring, the caret and text selection. A decorative third use breaks the system.

rules.name: The Falling Ground Rule
rules.body: Through the engine the ground's lightness only falls: bone, bone, figures, risk, parcel, ink, interpolated in OKLCH as each sheet lifts. Never lighten mid-dig. When the engine ends the page cuts back to bone in one step, and only the closing ask returns to ink.

rules.name: The Partner Tone Rule
rules.body: Every tone that sits on the ground has a dark partner, and the swap happens when ground lightness drops below 0.62: oxide to oxide-lit, ink-soft to on-dark-soft, rule to rule-dark, ink to on-dark.

rules.name: The Measured Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures carries everything measured or labelled: numbers, URLs, dates, gauge and spec labels, source captions, status lines and the scroll cue. A sentence of argument is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Light Serif Rule
rules.body: Newsreader stays at weight 350 to 400 with negative tracking (-0.012em to -0.035em) and an optical size matched to its size (48 to 72). The serif is never bold; emphasis comes from size and from the frame it is given.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: In the engine one frame holds one heading, one paragraph and one sheet. Copy crossfades with an 18px drift as the top sheet clears, so a heading is always on screen and two layers' copy never share it.

rules.name: The Paper Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is a pair: a 1 to 2px contact line plus a long, soft, negative-spread drop, tinted warm (hue 60) on bone. Only the ask button, on ink, uses neutral black. No hard offsets, no glows, no text shadows.

rules.name: The Pile Rule
rules.body: In the engine, depth is position. Each sheet under the top one sits 16px lower and 4% smaller with its own resting tilt (1.6, -1.2 and 1 degrees), and at most three show beneath. A sheet leaves by rising 108% of the viewport while turning -5 degrees, fading over the last 30% of its lift.

dos: Do keep oxide to the lit gauge tick and the Email me button, and borrow it only for the focus ring, caret and selection.
Do set every number, URL, date and label in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures.
Do swap to the partner tone (oxide-lit, on-dark-soft, rule-dark, on-dark) whenever ground lightness drops below 0.62.
Do use real captures (AVIF with a WebP fallback, at 2x) for product imagery, caption each with where it was captured, and draw data in HTML or SVG.
Do separate rows with 1px hairlines, open a group with a 1px ink rule, and close a total with a 3px double ink rule.
Do drive scroll motion with transform, opacity, filter and the one stage colour only, from a single rAF loop on scrollY, and use the exp curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for state transitions.
Do keep every interactive target at least 44px tall.
Do give reduced motion and screens under 560px tall the stacked fallback: every layer in order, each band in its own ground tone.
donts: Don't add a second accent colour or use oxide as decoration on borders, icons, headings or backgrounds.
Don't lighten the ground while digging down; the only lightening is the single cut back to bone after the engine.
Don't box projects in cards or tile them in a grid; in a ledger row the screenshot is the only object with radius and shadow.
Don't use generated or AI imagery anywhere; if it cannot be captured, draw it in HTML.
Don't set Newsreader bold or set prose in mono.
Don't use hard offset shadows, glows or text shadows.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading; labels belong to the gauge, the spec lists and the captions.
Don't round rows, bands or sections; radius belongs to pills (999px), sheets (18px) and screenshots (8px).
